subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and should this PR's opt-in minimal/standard/full semantics be the supported contract?
rationale: The implementation is plausible and proven, but choosing a new core config/default surface affects prompt context, session behavior, hook extras, upgrade expectations, and overlapping bootstrap-control proposals; automation should not settle that product contract.

options.title: Sponsor This Opt-In Tier Contract
options.body: Proceed with maintainer review of this PR as the focused additive path, requiring rebase, public docs, exact-head CI, and unchanged no-override defaults before merge.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Bootstrap Selection
options.body: Pause this PR and design one broader selector contract that covers tiering, per-session filtering, hook extras, and related prompt-pressure work together.

options.title: Decline The New Config Knob
options.body: Close or redirect the PR and steer users toward existing `contextInjection`, bootstrap budgets, lightweight mode, and narrower bug fixes instead of adding `bootstrapTier`.

recommendation.title: Sponsor This Opt-In Tier Contract
recommendation.body: Proceed with maintainer review of this PR as the focused additive path, requiring rebase, public docs, exact-head CI, and unchanged no-override defaults before merge.
